summary: This FTC press release, dated December 9, 2020, announces that the Federal Trade Commission sued Facebook for illegally maintaining a personal social networking monopoly through years of anticompetitive conduct. The complaint cites the Instagram acquisition ($1 billion, April 2012), the WhatsApp acquisition ($19 billion, announced February 2014), and restrictive API conditions imposed on third-party developers. The FTC seeks a permanent injunction that could require divestitures of Instagram and WhatsApp, and the vote to file was 3-2.
one_line: The FTC's December 2020 press release announcing its lawsuit accusing Facebook of illegally maintaining a personal social networking monopoly.
key_facts: The Federal Trade Commission sued Facebook on December 9, 2020, alleging it illegally maintains a personal social networking monopoly through a years-long course of anticompetitive conduct.
The investigation was conducted in cooperation with a coalition of attorneys general of 46 states, the District of Columbia, and Guam.
Facebook's acquisition of Instagram for $1 billion in April 2012 allegedly neutralized the direct threat posed by Instagram.
Facebook announced an agreement in February 2014 to acquire WhatsApp for $19 billion.

The complaint alleges Facebook made key APIs available to third-party applications only on the condition that they refrain from developing competing functionalities and from connecting with or promoting other social networking services.
In 2013, according to the complaint, Facebook shut down the API that would have allowed Twitter's app Vine to access friends via Facebook.
The FTC is seeking a permanent injunction that could require divestitures of assets, including Instagram and WhatsApp.

The requested relief could also prohibit Facebook from imposing anticompetitive conditions on software developers and require Facebook to seek prior notice and approval for future mergers and acquisitions.
Facebook generated revenues of more than $70 billion and profits of more than $18.5 billion in the last year, according to the FTC's complaint.
Ian Conner, Director of the FTC's Bureau of Competition, said: "Personal social networking is central to the lives of millions of Americans."
The Commission vote to authorize staff to file for a permanent injunction was 3-2, with Commissioners Noah Joshua Phillips and Christine S. Wilson voting no.
The complaint was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia.
The complaint alleges that by 2012 WhatsApp had emerged as the clear global "category leader" in mobile messaging.
The lawsuit followed an investigation by the FTC's Technology Enforcement Division, coordinated with the New York State Office of the Attorney General.
Media contact for the release was Betsy Lordan of the Office of Public Affairs.
